subject: Physics
subtopic: Uniformly Accelerated Linear Motion, Free Fall & 2D Projectile Motion
text: MoEYS Grade 12 Physics Chapter 1: Kinematics and Projectile Motion (ស៊ីនេម៉ាទិច និងចលនាគ្រាប់បាញ់). In 1D uniformly accelerated motion (ចលនាត្រង់ប្រែប្រួលស្មើ), acceleration a is constant, giving v = v_0 + at, x - x_0 = v_0 t + (1/2)at^2, and v^2 - v_0^2 = 2a(x - x_0). In 2D projectile motion (ចលនាគ្រាប់បាញ់) launched at speed v_0 and angle alpha above the horizontal under gravity g, horizontal motion is uniform (x = v_0 cos(alpha) t) while vertical motion is uniformly accelerated (y = v_0 sin(alpha) t - (1/2)gt^2).

metadata.starter_problem: v = v_0 + at, \quad v_0 = 0\text{ m/s}, \quad a = 2\text{ m/s}^2, \quad t = 5\text{ s}
learning_objectives: Solve 1D constant-acceleration and free-fall problems using the three kinematic equations
Decompose initial velocity v_0 into horizontal (v_0 cos alpha) and vertical (v_0 sin alpha) components
Derive and calculate time of flight T, maximum height H, and horizontal range R of a projectile

concepts.title: 1D Uniformly Accelerated Motion (ចលនាត្រង់ប្រែប្រួលស្មើ)
concepts.summary: Velocity-time, position-time, and time-independent kinematic equations.
concepts.body: When acceleration a is constant, velocity changes linearly with time (v = v_0 + at) and displacement is s = v_0 t + (1/2)at^2. Eliminating t yields v^2 - v_0^2 = 2as.

concepts.title: 2D Projectile Motion (ចលនាគ្រាប់បាញ់ក្នុងដែនទំនាញដី)
concepts.summary: Independent horizontal uniform motion and vertical free-fall motion.
concepts.body: Neglecting air resistance, a projectile has a_x = 0 and a_y = -g. The trajectory equation is y = -g x^2 / (2 v_0^2 cos^2 alpha) + x tan(alpha), a parabola.

formulas.name: 1D Constant Acceleration Kinematic Equations

formulas.name: Projectile Motion: Maximum Height, Time of Flight & Range

examples.problem: A car accelerates uniformly from rest at a = 2 m/s^2 for t = 5 s. Find its final velocity v and distance traveled s.
solution_steps: Step 1: Given v_0 = 0 m/s, a = 2 m/s^2, t = 5 s.
Step 2: Final velocity v = v_0 + at = 0 + 2(5) = 10 m/s.

examples.problem: A projectile is launched from the ground with v_0 = 20 m/s at angle alpha = 30 degrees (take g = 10 m/s^2). Find maximum height H and horizontal range R.
solution_steps: Step 2: Compute R = v_0^2 sin(60 deg) / g = 400 * (sqrt(3)/2) / 10 = 20 sqrt(3) m.

exercises.prompt: A stone is dropped from rest from a 45 m cliff (g = 10 m/s^2). Find the time to hit the ground and impact speed.
hints: Use h = (1/2)gt^2 to find t, then v = gt.

exercises.prompt: A car moving at 20 m/s brakes uniformly at a = -4 m/s^2 until stopping. Find the stopping distance.

solution_steps: Step 1: List known quantities (v_0, v, a, s, t) in SI units and choose a positive coordinate axis.
Step 2: Select the kinematic equation containing the 3 knowns and 1 unknown.
Step 3: Substitute numerical values and verify units.

common_misconceptions.text: Assuming total velocity v = 0 at the highest point of a 2D projectile trajectory.
common_misconceptions.correction: At the peak, only the vertical component v_y = 0; the horizontal velocity v_x = v_0 cos(alpha) remains constant and nonzero.

common_misconceptions.text: Using positive acceleration a = +g when an object is thrown upward with upward chosen as positive.
common_misconceptions.correction: Gravity always points downward; if upward is positive, a_y = -g throughout the entire flight.

subject: Physics
topic: Newton's Laws, Circular Motion and Gravitation
subtopic: Free-Body Diagrams, Friction, Centripetal Force & Universal Gravitation
text: MoEYS Grade 12 Physics Chapter 2: Dynamics, Uniform Circular Motion and Universal Gravitation (ឌីណាមិច ចលនាវង់ស្មើ និងទំនាញសកល). Newton's Second Law sum F = ma relates net force to acceleration. On an inclined plane at angle theta with kinetic friction mu_k, components are mg sin(theta) parallel and N = mg cos(theta) perpendicular. In uniform circular motion of radius r at speed v (angular speed omega = v/r), centripetal acceleration is a_c = v^2/r = omega^2 r and centripetal force is F_c = m v^2 / r. Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation is F_g = G m_1 m_2 / r^2, governing satellite orbits and Kepler's Third Law.

metadata.topic_khmer: ច្បាប់ញូតុន ចលនាវង់ និងទំនាញសកល

metadata.starter_problem: F_{\text{net}} = ma, \quad m = 5\text{ kg}, \quad F = 25\text{ N}, \quad f_k = 5\text{ N}
learning_objectives: Draw free-body diagrams and apply sum F = ma to blocks on horizontal and inclined planes with friction
Calculate angular velocity omega, centripetal acceleration a_c = v^2/r, and centripetal force F_c = mv^2/r
Apply Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation to determine orbital speed v = sqrt(GM/r) and period T

concepts.title: Newton's Second Law & Inclined Planes (ច្បាប់ទី២ញូតុន និងប្លង់ទម្រេត)
concepts.summary: Resolving weight mg into mg sin(theta) and mg cos(theta) with friction f_k = mu_k N.
concepts.body: For a mass m sliding down an incline of angle theta with coefficient of kinetic friction mu_k, the normal force is N = mg cos(theta), friction is f_k = mu_k mg cos(theta), and acceleration down the slope is a = g(sin theta - mu_k cos theta).

concepts.title: Uniform Circular Motion & Orbital Mechanics (ចលនាវង់ស្មើ និងចលនាផ្កាយរណប)
concepts.summary: Centripetal force F_c = mv^2/r and satellite orbital speed v = sqrt(GM/r).
concepts.body: A body moving in a circle of radius r at constant speed v experiences an inward centripetal acceleration a_c = v^2/r = omega^2 r. For a satellite orbiting Earth (mass M) at radius r, gravity provides the centripetal force: G M m / r^2 = m v^2 / r => v = sqrt(GM/r).

khmer_terms.Newton's Laws, Circular Motion and Gravi: ច្បាប់ញូតុន ចលនាវង់ និងទំនាញសកល

khmer_terms.normal force: កម្លាំងប្រតិកម្មកែង
khmer_terms.kinetic friction: កម្លាំងកកិតស៊ីនេទិច
khmer_terms.inclined plane: ប្លង់ទម្រេត
khmer_terms.uniform circular motion: ចលនាវង់ស្មើ
khmer_terms.centripetal acceleration: សំទុះផ្ចិត

formulas.name: Newton's Second Law & Inclined Plane Acceleration
Centripetal Acceleration & Force (សំទុះផ្ចិត និងកម្លាំងផ្ចិត)
formulas.expression: \omega = \frac{2\pi}{T} = 2\pi f, \quad v = \omega r, \quad a_c = \frac{v^2}{r} = \omega^2 r, \quad F_c = \frac{mv^2}{r}

formulas.name: Universal Gravitation & Satellite Orbital Speed

examples.problem: A 1000 kg car rounds a flat circular curve of radius r = 50 m at speed v = 15 m/s. Find the centripetal acceleration and the required friction force.
solution_steps: Step 1: Centripetal acceleration a_c = v^2 / r = 15^2 / 50 = 225 / 50 = 4.5 m/s^2.
Step 2: Centripetal force provided by static friction: F_c = m a_c = 1000 * 4.5 = 4500 N.

examples.problem: A 4 kg block is pulled across a horizontal surface by a 28 N horizontal force against a kinetic friction force of 8 N. Find its acceleration.
solution_steps: Step 1: Net horizontal force F_net = F - f_k = 28 - 8 = 20 N.
Step 2: Acceleration a = F_net / m = 20 / 4 = 5 m/s^2.

exercises.prompt: A 2 kg ball is whirled in a horizontal circle of radius 0.5 m at angular speed omega = 6 rad/s. Find the centripetal force.
A block slides down a frictionless incline of angle 30 degrees (g = 10 m/s^2). Find its acceleration.

solution_steps: Step 1: Draw a free-body diagram showing all real forces (gravity mg, normal N, tension T, friction f).
Step 2: Choose axes parallel and perpendicular to acceleration (radial inward for circular motion).
Step 3: Write sum F = ma along each axis and solve for the target unknown.

common_misconceptions.text: Treating centripetal force F_c as an extra separate force alongside tension, gravity, or friction on a free-body diagram.
common_misconceptions.correction: Centripetal force is the net radial force (sum F_r = mv^2/r) supplied by real forces such as tension, gravity, or friction.

common_misconceptions.text: Using N = mg on an inclined plane.
common_misconceptions.correction: On an incline of angle theta with no other vertical forces, N = mg cos(theta), not mg.

subject: Physics
topic: Kinetic Theory of Gases and Thermodynamics
subtopic: Ideal Gas Law, RMS Molecular Speed, First & Second Laws of Thermodynamics & Heat Engines
text: MoEYS Grade 12 Physics Unit 1: Kinetic Theory of Gases and Thermodynamics (ទ្រឹស្តីស៊ីនេទិចនៃឧស្ម័ន និងទែម៉ូឌីណាមិច). The Ideal Gas Law is PV = nRT = Nk_BT. From kinetic theory, pressure is P = (1/3)(N/V)m_0 v_rms^2, average translational kinetic energy per molecule is E_k = (3/2)k_B T, root-mean-square speed is v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M), and internal energy of a monatomic ideal gas is U = (3/2)nRT. The First Law of Thermodynamics states Delta U = Q - W (where W = P Delta V for isobaric expansion). For a heat engine operating between hot reservoir T_H and cold reservoir T_C, thermal efficiency is eta = W / Q_H = 1 - Q_C / Q_H, and Carnot maximum efficiency is eta_C = 1 - T_C / T_H.

metadata.topic_khmer: ទ្រឹស្តីស៊ីនេទិចនៃឧស្ម័ន និងទែម៉ូឌីណាមិច
metadata.subtopic_khmer: ឧស្ម័នបរិសុទ្ធ ល្បឿនមធ្យមការ៉េ ច្បាប់ទី១ និងទី២ទែម៉ូឌីណាមិច និងម៉ាស៊ីនកម្ដៅ
metadata.khmer_description: សិក្សាសមីការភាពនៃឧស្ម័នបរិសុទ្ធ PV = nRT ថាមពលស៊ីនេទិចមធ្យម និងល្បឿនមធ្យមការ៉េនៃម៉ូលេគុល ថាមពលក្នុង ច្បាប់ទី១ និងទី២នៃទែម៉ូឌីណាមិច និងទិន្នផលម៉ាស៊ីនកម្ដៅកាកណូ (Carnot)។
metadata.starter_problem: PV = nRT, \quad n = 2\text{ mol}, \quad T = 300\text{ K}, \quad V = 0.05\text{ m}^3, \quad \text{find } P
learning_objectives: Apply the Ideal Gas Equation PV = nRT in SI units (Pa, m^3, mol, K)
Calculate average molecular kinetic energy E_k = (3/2)k_B T, rms speed v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M), and internal energy U = (3/2)nRT
Analyze isochoric (V = const), isobaric (P = const), isothermal (T = const), and adiabatic (Q = 0) processes using the First Law Delta U = Q - W
Compute work output and thermal efficiency of heat engines and Carnot cycles

concepts.title: Kinetic Theory & Internal Energy of an Ideal Gas (ទ្រឹស្តីស៊ីនេទិច និងថាមពលក្នុង)
concepts.summary: Connecting macroscopic pressure and temperature to microscopic molecular motion.
concepts.body: Each molecule of an ideal gas has average translational kinetic energy E_k = (3/2)k_B T, which depends solely on absolute temperature T (in Kelvin). For n moles of a monatomic ideal gas, total internal energy is U = (3/2)nRT = (3/2)PV.

concepts.title: First & Second Laws of Thermodynamics (ច្បាប់ទី១ និងទី២ទែម៉ូឌីណាមិច)
concepts.summary: Conservation of energy Delta U = Q - W and Carnot heat engine efficiency.
concepts.body:
1. Isochoric (Delta V = 0): W = 0 => Delta U = Q.
2. Isobaric (P = const): W = P(V_2 - V_1) = nR(T_2 - T_1).
3. Isothermal (Delta T = 0): Delta U = 0 => Q = W = nRT ln(V_2/V_1).
4. Adiabatic (Q = 0): Delta U = -W.
5. Heat Engine: Q_H = W + Q_C, efficiency eta = W/Q_H = 1 - Q_C/Q_H <= 1 - T_C/T_H.

khmer_terms.Kinetic Theory of Gases and Thermodynami: ទ្រឹស្តីស៊ីនេទិចនៃឧស្ម័ន និងទែម៉ូឌីណាមិច

khmer_terms.root-mean-square speed: ល្បឿនមធ្យមការ៉េ
khmer_terms.internal energy: ថាមពលក្នុង
khmer_terms.first law of thermodynamics: ច្បាប់ទី១ទែម៉ូឌីណាមិច
khmer_terms.isothermal process: លំនាំអ៊ីសូទែម (T ថេរ)
khmer_terms.isobaric process: លំនាំអ៊ីសូបារ (P ថេរ)
khmer_terms.isochoric process: លំនាំអ៊ីសូករ (V ថេរ)
khmer_terms.adiabatic process: លំនាំអាដ្យាបាទិច (Q = 0)

khmer_terms.thermal efficiency: ទិន្នផលកម្ដៅ

prerequisites: Moles and molar mass M (kg/mol in SI)

formulas.name: Ideal Gas Law & Molecular Kinetic Formulas
formulas.expression: PV = nRT = Nk_B T, \quad \bar{E}_k = \frac{3}{2}k_B T, \quad v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}, \quad U = \frac{3}{2}nRT
formulas.conditions: Ideal gas; T in Kelvin and M in kg/mol for SI

formulas.name: First Law of Thermodynamics & Gas Work
formulas.expression: \Delta U = Q - W, \quad W_{\text{isobaric}} = P\Delta V, \quad W_{\text{isothermal}} = nRT\ln\left(\frac{V_2}{V_1}\right)
formulas.conditions: W > 0 when gas expands; Q > 0 when heat enters the system

formulas.name: Heat Engine & Carnot Efficiency (ទិន្នផលម៉ាស៊ីនកម្ដៅ)
formulas.conditions: T_H and T_C must be in Kelvin

examples.problem: A cylinder contains n = 2 mol of an ideal gas at T = 300 K in a volume V = 0.05 m^3 (R = 8.31 J/(mol K)). Find the pressure P and internal energy U (assuming monatomic gas).
solution_steps: Step 2: Internal energy of monatomic gas: U = (3/2)nRT = 1.5 * 2 * 8.31 * 300 = 7479 J.

examples.problem: An ideal Carnot heat engine operates between T_H = 500 K and T_C = 300 K, absorbing Q_H = 2000 J per cycle. Find its efficiency and work done per cycle.
solution_steps: Step 1: Carnot efficiency eta = 1 - T_C / T_H = 1 - 300/500 = 0.40 (40%).
Step 2: Work per cycle W = eta * Q_H = 0.40 * 2000 = 800 J.

exercises.prompt: A gas absorbs Q = 1500 J of heat while expanding and doing W = 600 J of work on its surroundings. Find the change in internal energy Delta U.
hints: Use the First Law of Thermodynamics Delta U = Q - W.

exercises.prompt: Calculate the rms speed of oxygen molecules (M = 32 g/mol = 0.032 kg/mol) at T = 300 K (R = 8.314 J/(mol K)).
hints: Convert M = 32 g/mol to 0.032 kg/mol before substituting into v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M).

solution_steps: Step 1: Convert all temperatures to Kelvin (T = t + 273.15), volumes to m^3, pressures to Pa, and molar mass to kg/mol.
Step 2: Identify the thermodynamic process (isochoric, isobaric, isothermal, adiabatic, or cyclic).
Step 3: Apply PV = nRT and Delta U = Q - W.

common_misconceptions.text: Substituting Celsius temperatures into PV = nRT or Carnot efficiency 1 - T_C/T_H.
common_misconceptions.correction: All gas law and thermodynamic efficiency equations require absolute temperature in Kelvin (K).

common_misconceptions.text: Using molar mass M in g/mol instead of kg/mol inside v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M).
common_misconceptions.correction: Because R = 8.314 J/(mol K) is in SI units (kg m^2 / s^2), M must be in kg/mol (e.g., 32 g/mol = 0.032 kg/mol).

subject: Physics
subtopic: Simple Harmonic Motion, Pendulums, Wave Propagation & Standing Waves
text: MoEYS Grade 12 Physics Unit 2: Mechanical Oscillations and Waves (លំយោលមេកានិច និងរលក). Simple harmonic motion (SHM, លំយោលអាម៉ូនិច) has displacement x(t) = A cos(omega t + phi), velocity v(t) = -omega A sin(omega t + phi), and acceleration a(t) = -omega^2 x(t). For a mass-spring system, omega = sqrt(k/m) and T = 2pi sqrt(m/k); for a simple pendulum, T = 2pi sqrt(L/g). A progressive wave of frequency f and speed v has wavelength lambda = v/f = vT. Superposition of two waves traveling in opposite directions creates standing waves (រលកជញ្ជ្រុំ) with nodes (ថ្នាំង) and antinodes (ពោះ) separated by lambda/2.

source.section: Simple Harmonic Motion, Pendulums, Wave Propagation & Standing Waves

Relate wave speed v, frequency f, period T, and wavelength lambda (v = lambda f)
Determine resonant wavelengths and frequencies of standing waves on a string fixed at both ends (L = n lambda / 2)

concepts.title: Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM) & Energy (លំយោលអាម៉ូនិច និងថាមពល)
concepts.summary: Kinematics and conservation of energy in mass-spring and simple pendulum systems.
concepts.body: In SHM, restoring force F = -kx produces a(t) = -omega^2 x(t). Maximum speed is v_max = omega A at equilibrium (x = 0), and maximum acceleration is a_max = omega^2 A at the turning points (x = +-A). Total mechanical energy E = (1/2)kA^2 = (1/2)mv^2 + (1/2)kx^2 is conserved.

concepts.title: Traveling Waves & Standing Waves (រលកដំណាល និងរលកជញ្ជ្រុំ)
concepts.summary: Wavelength lambda = v/f and resonance harmonics on strings and air columns.
concepts.body: A wave travels one wavelength lambda in one period T, so v = lambda / T = lambda f. On a string of length L fixed at both ends, standing waves form when L = n(lambda/2), giving harmonic frequencies f_n = n v / (2L) for n = 1, 2, 3, ... with n antinodes and (n + 1) nodes.

formulas.name: SHM Equations & Maximum Values

formulas.name: Spring Oscillator & Simple Pendulum Periods
Wave Speed & Standing Wave Harmonics on a Fixed String
formulas.expression: v = \lambda f = \frac{\lambda}{T}, \quad L = n\frac{\lambda_n}{2}, \quad f_n = n\frac{v}{2L} \quad (n = 1, 2, 3, \dots)

examples.problem: A harmonic oscillator has equation x(t) = 0.05\cos(10\pi t) (in meters and seconds). Find its amplitude A, frequency f, period T, and maximum speed v_{\max}.
examples.answer: A = 0.05\text{ m}, \quad f = 5\text{ Hz}, \quad T = 0.2\text{ s}, \quad v_{\max} = 0.5\pi \approx 1.57\text{ m/s}
solution_steps: Step 1: Compare with x(t) = A cos(omega t + phi): A = 0.05 m and omega = 10*pi rad/s.
Step 2: Frequency f = omega / (2pi) = 10*pi / (2pi) = 5 Hz, and period T = 1/f = 0.2 s.
Step 3: Maximum speed v_max = omega A = 10*pi * 0.05 = 0.5*pi m/s.

examples.problem: A string of length L = 1.2 m fixed at both ends vibrates in its 3rd harmonic (3 antinodes) at frequency f = 150 Hz. Find the wavelength and wave speed.
solution_steps: Step 1: For n = 3 fixed at both ends, L = 3(lambda / 2) => lambda = 2L / 3 = 2(1.2) / 3 = 0.8 m.
Step 2: Wave speed v = lambda * f = 0.8 * 150 = 120 m/s.

exercises.prompt: A 0.4 kg mass attached to a spring with k = 100 N/m oscillates with amplitude A = 0.1 m. Find the angular frequency omega and total mechanical energy E.
solution_steps: omega = sqrt(100 / 0.4) = sqrt(250) approx 15.81 rad/s.

exercises.prompt: A sound wave of frequency 680 Hz travels in air at 340 m/s. Find its wavelength.

solution_steps: Step 1: Extract A, omega, and phi from x(t) = A cos(omega t + phi).
Step 2: Use omega = 2*pi*f = 2*pi/T to link angular frequency, frequency, and period.
Step 3: For standing waves, count half-wavelengths (lambda/2) between adjacent nodes.

common_misconceptions.text: Thinking the distance between two adjacent nodes in a standing wave is one full wavelength lambda.
common_misconceptions.correction: Adjacent nodes (or adjacent antinodes) are separated by half a wavelength (lambda / 2); the distance between a node and the nearest antinode is lambda / 4.

common_misconceptions.text: Thinking the period of a simple pendulum depends on the mass of the bob.
common_misconceptions.correction: T = 2*pi*sqrt(L/g) depends only on length L and gravity g, not mass m.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Coulomb's Law, Electric Field & Potential, Capacitors & Ohm's Law
text: MoEYS Grade 12 Physics Unit 3: Electrostatics, Capacitors and Direct Current (អេឡិចត្រូស្តាទិច កុងដង់សាទ័រ និងចរន្តជាប់). Coulomb's Law gives the electrostatic force F = k|q_1 q_2|/r^2 (k = 9e9 N m^2/C^2), electric field E = F/q, and potential V = kq/r (with U_AB = E d in a uniform field). A capacitor has capacitance C = Q/U = epsilon_0 A / d and stores energy W = (1/2)CU^2 = (1/2)QU = Q^2/(2C). In DC circuits, Ohm's law for a complete circuit is I = E / (R + r), terminal voltage is U = E - Ir, and electrical power is P = UI = I^2 R.

concepts.title: Capacitors & Stored Electrostatic Energy (កុងដង់សាទ័រ និងថាមពលអគ្គិសនី)
concepts.summary: Capacitance C = Q/U, parallel-plate formula, and series/parallel combinations.
concepts.body: For capacitors in parallel, voltages are equal and C_eq = C_1 + C_2. For capacitors in series, charges Q are equal and 1/C_eq = 1/C_1 + 1/C_2. The energy stored in the electric field between the plates is W = (1/2)CU^2.

concepts.summary: Relating EMF E, internal resistance r, external load R, and current I.
concepts.body: A real voltage source with EMF E and internal resistance r connected to external resistance R drives current I = E / (R + r). The terminal voltage across the source is U = E - Ir = IR.

formulas.name: Coulomb's Law & Uniform Electric Field
formulas.expression: F = k\frac{|q_1 q_2|}{r^2}, \quad E = \frac{F}{|q|}, \quad U_{AB} = V_A - V_B = Ed
formulas.conditions: Point charges in vacuum/air; uniform field for U = Ed

formulas.name: Capacitance & Capacitor Energy
Ohm's Law for Complete Circuit & Electrical Power
formulas.expression: I = \frac{\mathcal{E}}{R + r}, \quad U = \mathcal{E} - Ir = IR, \quad P = UI = I^2 R

examples.problem: Two capacitors C_1 = 6\,\mu\text{F} and C_2 = 3\,\mu\text{F} are connected in series across a 12 V battery. Find the equivalent capacitance C_{\text{eq}}, charge Q on each capacitor, and total stored energy W.
solution_steps: Step 1: For two capacitors in series, C_eq = (C_1 * C_2)/(C_1 + C_2) = (6 * 3)/(6 + 3) = 2 uF.
Step 2: In series, both capacitors carry the same charge Q = C_eq * U = 2 uF * 12 V = 24 uC.
Step 3: Total energy W = (1/2) C_eq U^2 = 0.5 * 2 uF * 144 V^2 = 144 uJ.

examples.problem: A battery with EMF E = 12 V and internal resistance r = 1 Ohm is connected to an external resistor R = 5 Ohm. Find the current I and terminal voltage U.
solution_steps: Step 1: Apply Ohm's law for a complete circuit: I = E / (R + r) = 12 / (5 + 1) = 2 A.
Step 2: Terminal voltage U = E - Ir = 12 - 2(1) = 10 V (or U = IR = 2 * 5 = 10 V).

exercises.prompt: Find the energy stored in a 10\,\mu\text{F} capacitor charged to U = 100\text{ V}.
hints: Use W = (1/2)CU^2 with C = 10 x 10^{-6} F.

exercises.prompt: Two resistors R_1 = 6 Ohm and R_2 = 12 Ohm are connected in parallel across a 12 V source. Find the equivalent resistance and total current.
hints: Use R_eq = (R_1 R_2)/(R_1 + R_2) and I = U / R_eq.

solution_steps: Step 1: Convert microfarads (uF = 10^{-6} F) and microcoulombs (uC = 10^{-6} C) to SI units.
Step 2: Reduce series and parallel combinations step-by-step, noting that series elements share Q (or I) and parallel elements share U.
Step 3: Compute energy or power using the simplified circuit values.

common_misconceptions.text: Using the resistor series formula C_eq = C_1 + C_2 for capacitors in series.
common_misconceptions.correction: Capacitors combine oppositely to resistors: C_parallel = C_1 + C_2, whereas in series 1/C_eq = 1/C_1 + 1/C_2.

common_misconceptions.text: Forgetting to square the distance r in Coulomb's law F = k|q_1 q_2|/r^2.
common_misconceptions.correction: Coulomb's force obeys an inverse-square law with distance r.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Lorentz & Laplace Forces, Magnetic Flux, Faraday's Law, Lenz's Law & Inductance
text: MoEYS Grade 12 Physics Unit 4: Magnetic Fields and Electromagnetic Induction (ដែនម៉ាញេទិច និងអាំងឌុចស្យុងអេឡិចត្រូម៉ាញេទិច). Currents create magnetic fields: a straight wire gives B = 2e-7 I / r, and a solenoid gives B = mu_0 n I = 4pi e-7 (N/L) I. A magnetic field exerts the Laplace force F = B I L sin(theta) on a current-carrying wire and the Lorentz force F = |q| v B sin(theta) on a moving charge (causing circular motion of radius R = mv / (|q|B)). Magnetic flux through a coil is Phi = N B S cos(alpha). By Faraday's Law, a changing flux induces an EMF e = -Delta Phi / Delta t, whose direction opposes the change by Lenz's Law. Self-induced EMF in an inductor L is e_L = -L Delta I / Delta t.

concepts.title: Magnetic Forces: Laplace & Lorentz Forces (កម្លាំងឡាប្លាស និងកម្លាំងឡូរ៉ង់)
concepts.summary: Forces on current-carrying wires and moving charges in a magnetic field B.
concepts.body: A wire of length L carrying current I at angle theta to B experiences F = BIL sin(theta). A charge q moving at velocity v perpendicular to B experiences F = |q|vB perpendicular to v, doing zero work and bending the particle into a circle of radius R = mv/(|q|B).

concepts.title: Faraday's Law, Lenz's Law & Self-Induction (ច្បាប់ហ្វារ៉ាដេយ ច្បាប់ឡិន និងអូតូអាំងឌុចស្យុង)
concepts.summary: Induced EMF from changing magnetic flux and energy stored in an inductor.
concepts.body: Whenever the magnetic flux Phi = B S cos(alpha) through an N-turn coil changes, an induced EMF e = -N Delta Phi / Delta t is generated. In a coil of inductance L, changing current induces e_L = -L Delta I / Delta t and stores magnetic energy W_m = (1/2)LI^2.

Solenoid Field & Magnetic Flux

variables.alpha: Angle between normal vector n and B

formulas.name: Faraday's Law, Self-Induction & Inductor Energy

examples.problem: A coil of N = 200 turns has area S = 0.015 m^2 perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field that decreases from B_1 = 0.4 T to B_2 = 0 T in Delta t = 0.2 s. Find the magnitude of the induced EMF.
solution_steps: Step 1: Flux change per turn: Delta Phi = (B_2 - B_1) * S * cos(0 deg) = (0 - 0.4) * 0.015 = -0.006 Wb.
Step 2: Apply Faraday's Law: e = -N Delta Phi / Delta t = -200 * (-0.006) / 0.2 = 6 / 0.2 = 30 V.

examples.problem: An inductor of inductance L = 0.5 H carries a steady current I = 4 A. Find the magnetic energy stored in the inductor and the self-induced EMF if the current drops to 0 in 0.1 s.
solution_steps: Step 1: Stored magnetic energy W_m = (1/2)LI^2 = 0.5 * 0.5 * 4^2 = 4 J.
Step 2: Self-induced EMF e_L = -L (0 - 4) / 0.1 = 20 V.

exercises.prompt: A straight wire of length L = 0.5 m carrying current I = 6 A is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B = 0.4 T. Find the Laplace force on the wire.
A long solenoid of length L = 0.5 m has N = 1000 turns and carries current I = 2 A. Calculate the magnetic field B inside its center.

solution_steps: Step 1: Carefully identify the angle alpha between the coil normal vector n and B (not between the coil plane and B).
Step 2: Compute initial and final magnetic flux Phi = BS cos(alpha).
Step 3: Apply Faraday's law e = -N Delta Phi / Delta t and Ohm's law I = |e| / R.

common_misconceptions.text: Using the angle between B and the plane of the loop directly inside Phi = BS cos(alpha).
common_misconceptions.correction: alpha in Phi = BS cos(alpha) is the angle between B and the unit normal vector n perpendicular to the loop surface.

common_misconceptions.text: Thinking a strong static magnetic field always induces a current in a stationary loop.
common_misconceptions.correction: Induced EMF requires a changing magnetic flux (Delta Phi != 0); a constant flux produces zero induced EMF.

subject: Physics
topic: Alternating Current (AC) RLC Circuits and Transformers
subtopic: RMS Values, Reactance, Impedance, Resonance, Power Factor & Transformers
text: MoEYS Grade 12 Physics Unit 4 (AC Circuits): Alternating Current RLC Series Circuits and Transformers (ចរន្តឆ្លាស់ សៀគ្វី RLC និងត្រង់ស្វូម៉ាទ័រ) — a guaranteed problem on every BacII Physics exam. For sinusoidal AC i(t) = I_m cos(omega t) and u(t) = U_m cos(omega t + phi), effective (RMS) values are I = I_m / sqrt(2) and U = U_m / sqrt(2). In a series RLC circuit, inductive reactance is X_L = omega L, capacitive reactance is X_C = 1/(omega C), total impedance is Z = sqrt(R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2), Ohm's law is I = U/Z, phase angle satisfies tan(phi) = (X_L - X_C)/R, power factor is cos(phi) = R/Z, and average active power is P = U I cos(phi) = R I^2. Electrical resonance occurs when X_L = X_C (omega_0 = 1/sqrt(LC)), minimizing Z = R and maximizing current I_max = U/R.

metadata.khmer_description: សិក្សាចរន្តឆ្លាស់ស៊ីនុសអ៊ីដាល់ សៀគ្វី RLC តជាស៊េរី (រេអាក់តង់ អាំងប៉េដង់ Z គម្លាតផាស កត្តាអានុភាព បាតុភូតរេសូណង់អគ្គិសនី) និងត្រង់ស្វូម៉ាទ័រ។
metadata.starter_problem: R = 30\,\Omega, \quad X_L = 60\,\Omega, \quad X_C = 20\,\Omega \text{ in series. Find impedance } Z.
learning_objectives: Convert between peak (U_m, I_m) and effective RMS values (U = U_m/sqrt(2), I = I_m/sqrt(2))
Compute inductive reactance X_L = omega L, capacitive reactance X_C = 1/(omega C), and total impedance Z = sqrt(R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2)
Determine the phase difference phi between u(t) and i(t), the power factor cos(phi) = R/Z, and average power P = UI cos(phi)
Analyze electrical resonance (X_L = X_C, omega_0 = 1/sqrt(LC)) and ideal transformer ratios U_2/U_1 = N_2/N_1 = I_1/I_2

concepts.title: Series RLC Impedance, Phasors & Power (អាំងប៉េដង់ គម្លាតផាស និងអានុភាពមធ្យម)
concepts.summary: Combining R, X_L, and X_C using Fresnel phasor vectors.
concepts.body: In a series RLC circuit, u_R is in phase with i, u_L leads i by pi/2, and u_C lags i by pi/2. Thus U = sqrt(U_R^2 + (U_L - U_C)^2) and Z = sqrt(R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2). Only the resistor dissipates average real power: P = U I cos(phi) = R I^2.

concepts.title: Electrical Resonance & Transformers (រេសូណង់អគ្គិសនី និងត្រង់ស្វូម៉ាទ័រ)
concepts.summary: Resonance condition X_L = X_C and transformer voltage/current transformation.
concepts.body: At resonance X_L = X_C => omega_0 = 1/sqrt(LC), impedance reaches its minimum Z = R, phase angle phi = 0 (cos phi = 1), and current is maximum I = U/R. For an ideal transformer, U_2 / U_1 = N_2 / N_1 = I_1 / I_2.

formulas.name: Phase Angle, Power Factor & Average Power

variables.phi: Phase angle of voltage relative to current

formulas.name: Resonance Frequency & Ideal Transformer Law

examples.problem: A series RLC circuit has R = 30 Ohm, X_L = 60 Ohm, and X_C = 20 Ohm connected across an AC source of RMS voltage U = 100 V. Find the impedance Z, RMS current I, power factor cos(phi), and average power P.
examples.answer: Z = 50 Ohm, I = 2 A, cos(phi) = 0.6, P = 120 W
solution_steps: Step 1: Compute impedance Z = sqrt(R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2) = sqrt(30^2 + (60 - 20)^2) = sqrt(900 + 1600) = 50 Ohm.
Step 2: RMS current I = U / Z = 100 / 50 = 2 A.
Step 3: Power factor cos(phi) = R / Z = 30 / 50 = 0.6.
Step 4: Average power P = U I cos(phi) = 100 * 2 * 0.6 = 120 W (or P = R I^2 = 30 * 4 = 120 W).

examples.problem: An ideal step-down transformer has N_1 = 1000 primary turns and N_2 = 100 secondary turns. If the primary is connected to U_1 = 220 V and the secondary delivers I_2 = 5 A, find U_2 and I_1.
solution_steps: Step 1: Secondary voltage U_2 = U_1 * (N_2 / N_1) = 220 * (100 / 1000) = 22 V.
Step 2: Primary current I_1 = I_2 * (N_2 / N_1) = 5 * 0.1 = 0.5 A.

exercises.prompt: Find the capacitance C required to produce electrical resonance with an inductor L = \frac{1}{\pi}\text{ H} at angular frequency \omega = 100\pi\text{ rad/s}.
hints: At resonance X_C = X_L, so 1/(omega C) = omega L => C = 1/(omega^2 L).
solution_steps: X_L = omega L = (100*pi)*(1/pi) = 100 Ohm.
At resonance X_C = 100 Ohm => C = 1 / (100*pi * 100) = 10^{-4}/pi F.

exercises.prompt: An AC voltage is given by u(t) = 220\sqrt{2}\cos(100\pi t)\text{ V}. State its RMS voltage U and frequency f.
hints: Use U = U_m / sqrt(2) and f = omega / (2pi).

solution_steps: Step 1: Calculate X_L = omega L and X_C = 1/(omega C) in Ohms.
Step 2: Compute total impedance Z = sqrt(R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2) and RMS current I = U/Z.
Step 3: Find phase angle phi from tan(phi) = (X_L - X_C)/R and power from P = UI cos(phi).

common_misconceptions.text: Adding impedance algebraically as Z = R + X_L + X_C.
common_misconceptions.correction: Because resistor and inductor/capacitor voltages are 90 degrees out of phase, impedance must be combined using the Pythagorean phasor formula Z = sqrt(R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2).

common_misconceptions.text: Using peak voltage U_m instead of RMS voltage U in P = U I cos(phi).
common_misconceptions.correction: Average AC power P = U I cos(phi) uses effective (RMS) values U = U_m/sqrt(2) and I = I_m/sqrt(2).

subject: Physics
topic: Wave Optics, Quantum Physics and Nuclear Physics
subtopic: Young's Double-Slit Interference, Photoelectric Effect, Mass Defect & Radioactive Decay
text: MoEYS Grade 12 Physics Units 5 & 6: Wave Optics, Quantum Physics and Nuclear Physics (អុបទិចរលក រូបវិទ្យាកង់ទិច និងរូបវិទ្យានុយក្លេអ៊ែរ). In Young's double-slit experiment (ពិសោធន៍យ៉ាំង), fringe spacing is i = lambda D / a, with bright fringes at x_k = k i and dark fringes at x_k = (k + 1/2)i. In quantum physics, a photon has energy E = hf = hc/lambda; Einstein's photoelectric equation is hf = W_0 + E_{k,max} where W_0 = hc/lambda_0 is the work function and lambda_0 is the threshold wavelength. In nuclear physics, mass defect is Delta m = [Z m_p + (A - Z)m_n] - m_X, binding energy is E_b = Delta m c^2, and radioactive decay follows N(t) = N_0 2^{-t/T} = N_0 e^{-lambda t}.

metadata.starter_problem: i = \frac{\lambda D}{a}, \quad \lambda = 600\text{ nm}, \quad D = 2\text{ m}, \quad a = 1\text{ mm. Find fringe spacing } i.
learning_objectives: Calculate fringe width i = lambda D / a and positions of bright and dark fringes in Young's double-slit experiment
Apply Einstein's photoelectric equation hf = W_0 + (1/2)m v_max^2 = W_0 + eU_s

concepts.title: Young's Double-Slit Interference & Photoelectric Effect (អាំងទែផេរ៉ង់ និងផូតូអគ្គិសនី)
concepts.summary: Wave nature of light (i = lambda D / a) and particle nature of light (hf = W_0 + E_k,max).
concepts.body: Two coherent slits separated by distance a at distance D from a screen produce equally spaced interference fringes with spacing i = lambda D / a. Conversely, photoemission occurs only when photon wavelength lambda <= lambda_0 (threshold wavelength), with maximum photoelectron kinetic energy E_{k,max} = hc/lambda - hc/lambda_0.

concepts.title: Nuclear Binding Energy & Radioactive Decay (ថាមពលសម្ព័ន្ធនុយក្លេអ៊ែរ និងវិទ្យុសកម្ម)
concepts.summary: Mass-energy equivalence E = Delta m c^2 and exponential decay law N = N_0 2^{-t/T}.
concepts.body: The mass of a stable nucleus is always less than the sum of its constituent protons and neutrons; this mass defect Delta m corresponds to binding energy E_b = Delta m * 931.5 MeV. Unstable nuclei decay with half-life T such that after n = t/T half-lives, N = N_0 / 2^n.

prerequisites: Scientific notation and eV <-> Joule conversion (1 eV = 1.6e-19 J)

formulas.name: Young's Double-Slit Interference Formulas
Einstein's Photoelectric Equation
formulas.expression: E = hf = \frac{hc}{\lambda}, \quad hf = W_0 + E_{k,\max} = \frac{hc}{\lambda_0} + eU_s

formulas.name: Nuclear Binding Energy & Radioactive Half-Life Law
formulas.expression: \Delta m = Z m_p + (A - Z)m_n - m_X, \quad E_b = \Delta m c^2, \quad N(t) = N_0 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/T}

examples.problem: In a Young's double-slit experiment, slit separation is a = 1 mm, screen distance is D = 2 m, and light wavelength is lambda = 600 nm. Find the fringe spacing i and the position of the 4th bright fringe.
solution_steps: Step 1: Convert to SI units: lambda = 600e-9 m = 6e-7 m, a = 1e-3 m, D = 2 m.
Step 2: Fringe spacing i = lambda D / a = (6e-7 * 2) / 1e-3 = 1.2e-3 m = 1.2 mm.
Step 3: Position of 4th bright fringe (k = 4): x_4 = 4 * i = 4 * 1.2 mm = 4.8 mm.

examples.problem: A radioactive sample has a half-life of T = 8 days and initial mass m_0 = 64 g. How much undecayed mass remains after t = 24 days?
solution_steps: Step 1: Number of half-lives n = t / T = 24 / 8 = 3.
Step 2: Remaining mass m = m_0 / 2^n = 64 / 2^3 = 64 / 8 = 8 g.

exercises.prompt: A metal has work function W_0 = 2.2 eV. If it is illuminated by photons of energy E = 3.5 eV, find the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons in eV.
A radioactive isotope decays to 1/16 of its original activity in 40 minutes. Find its half-life T.
solution_steps: n = 4 half-lives in 40 minutes => T = 40 / 4 = 10 minutes.
Step 1: For optics, convert nm (10^{-9} m) and mm (10^{-3} m) to meters before computing i = lambda D / a.
Step 2: For photoelectric problems, keep energies consistently in eV or convert using 1 eV = 1.6e-19 J.
Step 3: For radioactivity, compute the number of half-lives n = t/T and apply N = N_0 / 2^n.

common_misconceptions.text: Thinking higher light intensity increases the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons.
common_misconceptions.correction: Higher intensity increases photon count (and thus photocurrent), whereas E_{k,max} = hf - W_0 depends only on photon frequency f.

common_misconceptions.text: Assuming all radioactive atoms vanish after two half-lives (2T).
common_misconceptions.correction: Each half-life halves the remaining amount: after 2T, (1/2)^2 = 1/4 (25%) of the original nuclei still remain.
